properties.description:
At 258 PM EDT, a confirmed tornado was located near Wyse Fork, or 10
miles southeast of Kinston, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Damaging tornado.

SOURCE...Radar confirmed tornado.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

This tornado will be near...
Wyse Fork around 305 PM EDT.
Fort Barnwell around 320 PM EDT.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include Dover
and Cove City.
properties.instruction:
To repeat, a tornado is on the ground. TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a
basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy
building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in
a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect
yourself from flying debris.

If a tornado or other severe weather is spotted, report it to the
National Weather Service or your local nearest law enforcement agency
who will send your report. This act may save lives of others in the
path of dangerous weather.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Ashe County in northwestern North Carolina...

* IMPACTS...Flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Strong
flows over low-water crossings will continue through the middle of
the afternoon, especially those along the Watauga River in western

afternoon, however water remains over a few roadways, including
Todd Railroad Grade Road along the South Fork of the New River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 251 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
that rain has exited the advisory area. However, minor flooding
continues due to between 4 and 7 inches of rain that fell from
Saturday morning through this morning.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Brushy Fork, Call Creek, Beaverdam Creek, Cove Creek, Beech
Creek, Big Horse Creek, Big Laurel Creek and Beaver Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Jefferson, West Jefferson, Beech Mountain, Lansing, Ashland,
Glendale Springs and Sugar Grove.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather Service
by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports and
pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.areaDesc: Buchanan
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 11 at 2:24PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
Locations impacted include...
Stacy.

Heavy rain may cause ponding of water on roadways and water issues
in low-lying areas. Motorists should exercise extreme caution and be
prepared for water on roadways.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to travel across
flooded roads. Find alternate routes. It takes only a few inches of
swiftly flowing water to carry vehicles away.

NWSheadline: HEAVY RAIN WILL AFFECT CENTRAL BUCHANAN COUNTY

properties.areaDesc: Hendry; Inland Collier County
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 11 at 2:23PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
At 222 PM EDT, National Weather Service meteorologists were tracking
a strong thunderstorm 12 miles south of Ave Maria, moving northeast
at 5 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 45 to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Hendry Correctional, Miles City, and Sunniland.
properties.instruction:
These winds can down small tree limbs and branches, and blow around
unsecured small objects. Seek shelter in a safe building until the
storm passes.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets
and lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.
properties.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT

properties.areaDesc: Washington, UT
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 12:18PM MDT until October 11 at 3:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Forsyth burn scar in...
Central Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 315 PM MDT.

* At 1218 PM MDT, Emergency management reported heavy rain over the
Forsyth Burn Scar, and river gauges are rising rapidly along the
Santa Clara River. Between 1.25 and 2.25 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other
loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Forsyth Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Forsyth Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pine Valley.

This includes Utah Route 18 between mile markers 26 and 27.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Forsyth Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:15 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:15 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.areaDesc: Kaibab Plateau; Marble and Glen Canyons; Grand Canyon Country; Coconino Plateau; Yavapai County Mountains; Western Mogollon Rim; Eastern Mogollon Rim; Northern Gila County; Yavapai County Valleys and Basins; Oak Creek and Sycamore Canyons
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 11:08AM MST until October 12 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...western Coconino, northern Gila, far southern Navajo, and
Yavapai counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Numerous showers and thunderstorms are expected to continue
across the area through tonight. With tropical moisture in place
from the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel, periods of embedded
heavy rainfall will be possible this afternoon which could lead
to flash flooding. Additionally, the extended period of rain
could lead to elevated flow in creeks, normally dry washes, and
rivers.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

* WHERE...All of central and northern Arizona.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST /9 PM MDT/ this evening.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
